audit.method: Read-only offline hash verification, fixed git blob comparison, independent literal wire/finite-offset/raw exit/primary/native state/cleanup assertions; no build or product test rerun.

originalCondition: 无变化不输出；部分写失败不提交基线，安全重同步后完整重绘；无法确认时停止输出并报错
scope: Complete original AC008 under current M1 C002/S008 Linux output contract, choosing explicit stop/report after partial fatal output.

conditions.reason: Equal projected rows produce no grid output; the successful visible caret baseline suppresses redundant CUP. Normal frame/style/caret/title/clipboard invalidation fences assert zero additional transactions; identical Monochrome profile remains silent. Original normal-caret RED is 4 to 5 transactions, fixed is 4 to 4.

The normal-caret wire is initial full grid plus CUP to (0,0), then a standalone CUP to (2,0), with unchanged target silence. For every visible caret, nonempty grid output makes the OR condition true, so CUP is appended after grid bytes regardless of whether the logical caret changed. This covers both full and differential grid branches.
conditions.limit: The dedicated unchanged-logical-caret/profile attempt did not generate a grid rewrite. It is not counted as a positive runtime case. Exact source branch proof plus literal initial-grid/CUP and movement controls is sufficient for this condition; no missing current contract requirement is deferred.

conditions.reason: Independent literal bytes show shortened text erases the old tail, RGB+bold style-only updates, Monochrome removes RGB while retaining bold, and coherent 4 to 2 to 4 dimensions repaint full rows. The unique frame backend compares old/new projected profiles.

Frame, immutable caret, visibility probe, profile, glyph mode and dimensions are assigned only in the committed branch after write success. Fatal write records the first error and throws before commit; cancellation breaks; allocation failure clears frame baseline. The runtime returns a copy of its cached target, preventing old Frame aliasing. Empty output commits an equivalent device state safely.
conditions.limit: RuntimeStats.frames counts generated targets and is not used as a successful-device-commit oracle. Fatal-stop policy prevents a legal same-run follow-up present, so source ordering is the baseline proof and raw stop evidence is its observable corroboration.

conditions.reason: The native allocation seam emits no candidate bytes, clears baseline and retries a complete 4-cell target. Five scenario pairs separately prove one-byte positive short-write completion and EINTR retry; actual wire equals every complete candidate byte and unsafe remains clear.
conditions.limit: Allocation evidence covers the native buffer seam, not arbitrary managed-heap OOM recovery.

conditions.reason: All 320 finite cases independently reasserted: 13 actual transaction families times EIO/zero-return, every offset 0 through length-1. Families cover shortened/full UTF8 grid, SGR, CUP, paste enable, DECRQM query, caret hide, title save/set/restore, OSC52 clipboard, paste restore and caret restore. Each selected candidate matches a fixed literal; each actual wire equals its legal prefix with only safe zero-failure cleanup/reopen bytes.

Every partial fatal record has exact positive emitted count and unsafe=1, no later transaction or actual byte, no post-fault poll, exact ParserUnsynchronized error (title cleanup retains its specified restore error), native cleanup and same-process reopen refusal. The process-lifetime latch blocks writer/open and is not reset on close. No safe real-TTY resynchronization is claimed or needed: the contract permits explicit stop when safety cannot be confirmed.

Every offset-zero EIO/zero-return records emitted=0 and unsafe=0, reports the exact first error, ends the current run without polling again, restores safe modes/native state and permits the tested next run. Safe cleanup bytes are distinguished from forbidden continuing frame/input processing.

All 338 raw cases have direct consumer wait exit0, finished=true, no signal/forced kill, exact termios equality, three restored signal handlers/masks, native close, UI cleanup once and public resources 0/0/0/0. The combined failure case retains device primary followed by exact UI and native cleanup extras. Native close restores and frees without output. Existing accepted S152 business-primary/callback/multiple-cleanup evidence is reused with its original limits.
conditions.limit: Injected native-close return failure occurs after real close; this is not proof of an actual OS tcsetattr failure. The protocol stop is supported by raw wire/native logs and the direct consumer exit chain, not by generated-frame counts.
